To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated synthetic NDVI time series from MODIS and Landsat data and used the data to estimate biomass and detect anomalies in grasslands.
the synthetic NDVIderived estimations contained more detail on the distribution and the severity of vegetation anomalies, compared with MODIS-NDVI derived AGB estimation.

We generated a time series of biomass data for grasslands in Inner Mongolia using a data fusion approach and an SVM AGB model, which has improved spatial and temporal resolutions and is useful for monitoring grassland conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new data fusion method and a new AGB model to generate high spatial (30 m resolution) and temporal (8 d resolution) biomass data for grassland regions in China.
a novel method for generating synthetic NDVI time series with fine spatial and temporal resolutions.
developing an improved method for monitoring grassland biomass at fine spatial and temporal resolutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study is the first to develop an SVM AGB model to estimate biomass from synthetic NDVI data and to detect biomass anomalies in grassland regions.
our study is the first time to apply synthetic NDVI time series derived from Landsat and Modis data for grassland biomass estimation.

the synthetic NDVIs derived from Landsat and Moderate Resolution Imaging SpectroRadiometer (MODIS), and the SVM ACG model can be effectively applied to generate grassland biomass maps with high spatial (30 m), temporal (8 d), and temporal resolution (1 month) for the study region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can provide a more accurate and timely estimation of biomass for grassland ecosystems with 30 m 8 d intervals.
we have generated a new time series biomass dataset for grassland regions, and this has been done for the first time in China.

the synthetic NDVIs derived from the data fusion method can be used to generate high resolution (30 m) biomass maps, and the biomass estimation model (SVC AGB) can be used to detect grassland biomass anomalies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthetic NDVISVM AGB model can be used to generate high resolution biomass time series data, which will be useful to detect biomass anomalies and to monitor grassland dynamics.

the data fusion approach can be used for improving the accuracy of biomass estimations and for monitoring vegetation changes in arid and semi-arid grasslands with 30 m spatial and 8 d temporal resolution.
the combination of the SVM AGB and STARFM can be used for generating time series biomass maps with 30 m spatial and 8 d temporal resolution.
